LESSON: GUIDED WRITING: SYMBOLS/CHARACTERS OF THE ALPHABET

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Writing
Topic 3.2: Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet, part of Writing in Grade 5 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you develop a good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. blend letters/ syllables to form words,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. copy words and sentences accurately,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. blend letters/ syllables to form words,

   Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. copy words and sentences accurately,

   Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the characters of the Arabic Alphabet.

   Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. work jointly to match sounds to letters and blend letters and syllables to form words,

2. trace words related to the theme accurately,

3. re-write the simple Arabic greetings and introduction neatly,

4. work collaboratively to match simple greetings to their responses,

5. practise greetings with peers and parents.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. work jointly to match sounds to letters and blend letters and syllables to form words,
2. trace words related to the theme accurately,
3. re-write the simple Arabic greetings and introduction neatly,
4. work collaboratively to match simple greetings to their responses,
5. practise greetings with peers and parents.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Guided Writing: Symbols/Characters of the Alphabet together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner practises greetings with peers and parents.

Learning to learn: This is promoted as the learner engages in collective learning when working collaboratively to match simple

greetings to their responses.

and blend letters and syllables to form words.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

introductions.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate this concept on greetings and introduction to similar concepts as taught in all other languages.
